Subject: Prism POC: recommended model slate + validation sprint proposal

Thanks again for your time today — great conversation and helpful context on the multi-tenant support and 95th-percentile latency target (sub-200ms for single-shot queries). Per our demo and the sample prompts you shared, we've pulled together a recommended shortlist and a pragmatic validation plan so Prism can make a deterministic tradeoff decision between cost and tail latency.

High-level recommendation (shortlist):
- variant-A: LlamaX-13B-q4f (production starter) — best cost/perf for typical prompt lengths (<=256 tokens). Expected median latency ~90ms, 95th ~180ms on same host profile; cost estimate $0.025 / 1k tokens.
- variant-B: Mistral-30B-int8 (quality-first) — stronger on long-context summarization and extractive Q&A; median ~140ms, 95th ~260ms; cost estimate $0.08 / 1k tokens.
- variant-C: Llama2-70B-qat (fallback/high-quality) — highest fidelity, good for policy-sensitive responses; median ~250ms, 95th ~420ms; cost estimate $0.18 / 1k tokens.

Why these three?
- Coverage across your main axes: cost (A), latency/SLAs (A+B combination), and top-end quality for edge-case legal summarization (C).
- We measured regressions on your prompt pack (attached) vs. Redwood baseline: A shows negligible semantic drift, B improves factuality on multi-hop items, C reduces hallucination risk on red-team prompts.

Validation sprint proposal (2 weeks):
1) Run deterministic evals we discussed: throughput and p95 latency under representative qps (10, 50, 200) using your sample prompt sets (attached).
2) Quality regressions: run the regression harness (we'll provide) against your curated 200-case prompt set and flag any >5% semantic-f1 drop.
3) Cost model: estimate per-route unit economics with caching and batching suggestions enabled.
4) Fallback playbook: define automatic fallback rules (A->B->C) and degrade gracefully to smaller responses if tail latency is breached.

Attachments: prism_demo_benchmarks.csv, prompt_pack_v1.txt, demo_recording_prism_apr25.mp4. HubSpot link and Drive folder below.

Next steps we propose:
- Confirm you want Redwood to run the 2-week validation sprint (we can start Mon 4/26).
- If yes, share an ETA for procurement/PO route — Connor will lead the ingestion of contract/PO requirements.

Happy to hop on a quick call to walk through the benchmark CSV.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks Jasmine — this is super helpful. A few quick clarifying Qs before we greenlight the sprint:
1) For the LlamaX-13B-q4f (A), you note negligible semantic drift — can you share the exact metrics you used (BLEU/F1/semantic-similarity) and a short example where A failed vs B?
2) We care a lot about recall on entity extraction (legal names/clauses). Does the regression harness include entity-level recall?
3) On procurement — we'll need an estimate for a limited SLA (uptime + 95th latency guarantee) to get internal buy-in. Is that something you can surface for a 30-day trial?

If you can answer those two items today we'll push to approve the sprint.

Elliot — quick answers and data snippets below. Happy to expand in a call.

Metrics and examples:
- Semantic similarity: we use a combination of SBERT cosine (sentence-level) plus a domain-aware entailment model we maintain. For the CSV attached, 'semantic-f1' is average of thresholded entailment + normalized SBERT. For A vs B: one failure case in the pack (contract clause paraphrase) where A returned a concise but incomplete extraction; SBERT drop ~0.12, entailment score drop 0.18. I've added the example row in prism_demo_benchmarks.csv (row 87) and tagged it 'edge-extraction-failure'.
- Entity recall: yes — the harness includes entity-level recall/precision for named-entities relevant to your domain. We score entity-match with normalized token overlap + fuzzy group dedup. For your 200-case pack, current passes: A=88% recall, B=94%, C=97% on the entity set.

SLA/30-day trial estimate:
- For a capped trial (single dedicated vCPU pool + reserved GPU capacity for peak windows) we can offer a trial SLA with a p95 latency objective and credits for measured misses. I'll have Connor pull the pricing delta; rough delta to enable p95-backed monitoring and incident crediting is ~+$3k/mo on top of usage for this workload profile. We can convert to a short-term trial quote for approvals.

Notes on quantization and quality:
- LlamaX-13B-q4f uses aggressive q4f quantization; generally minimal semantic loss on short prompts but more brittle on long-context legal paraphrase. That's why the fallback chain is important.
- Mistral-30B-int8 shows stronger long-context coherence; downside is higher cost and slightly higher tail latency.

Proposed immediate actions if Prism approves sprint:
- Start perf runs for qps=[10,50,200] this week; deliver baseline CSV and a short executive slide.
- Run the regression harness and return a list of flagged prompts and recommended mitigations (prompt tweaks, context window tuning, caching).

I'll attach a small excerpt from the benchmark CSV to this thread for visibility.

-Karthik

Quick ops/guardrail notes from my side:
- Prompt pack: please include the red-team set (we flagged 12 high-risk prompts) — I put the red-team examples into prompt_pack_v1.txt under folder /red-team. We'll surface recommended sanitization templates where necessary.
- Quantization QA: when we run A at scale, let's also run a 10% sample at float16 to confirm no silent regressions. We'll log diffs at the token level for audit.
- Fallback timing: suggest a 250ms p95 cutoff for auto-fallback A->B for your SLA profile; for user-facing legal extractions we recommend manual review on any flagged low-confidence extractions.

I'll draft a 1-page ops runbook and share by EOD tomorrow.
